'''Xukuru''' (Xucuru, Shukurú, Ichikile, {{langx|xoo|Brobo}}<ref name="Meader-Nordeste">{{cite book |last=Meader |first=Robert E. |url=https://www.silbrazil.org/resources/archives/16988 |title=Indios do Nordeste: Levantamento sobre os remanescentes tribais do nordeste brasileiro |year=1978 |publisher=[[SIL International]] |location=Brasilia |lang=pt |archive-date=2024-10-08 |access-date=2020-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008181259/https://www.silbrazil.org/resources/archives/16988 |url-status=dead }}</ref>) is a poorly attested [[extinct language]] of Brazil. It is known only from a few word lists and a sketch by [[Geraldo Lapenda]] (1962).<ref name="Lapenda-Xucuru">Lapenda, Geraldo Calábria. 1962. [http://biblio.etnolinguistica.org/lapenda_1962_xucuru O dialecto Xucuru]. ''Doxa'' (Revista Oficial do Departamento de Cultura do Diretório Acadêmico da Faculdade de Filosofia de Pernambuco da Universidade do Recife), ano X, n. 10, p. 11-23.</ref>

It was originally spoken in the Serra de São José and on the [[Do Meio River (Paraíba)|Meio River]], [[Capibaribe River]] and [[Taperoa River]] in the states of [[Pernambuco]] and [[Paraíba]]. Loukotka (1968) reports the most recent locations as the [[:pt:Serra do Ororubá|Serra Ararobá]] and [[Pesqueira, Pernambuco|Pesqueira]] (formerly Cimbres).<ref name="Loukotka"/>

==Classification==
Loukotka (1968) considers Xukurú to form a [[Xukuru languages|small family]] with [[Paratió language|Paratió]] and the unattested Garanhun (Garañun).<ref name="Loukotka">{{cite book |last=Loukotka |first=Čestmír |authorlink=Čestmír Loukotka |title=Classification of South American Indian languages |url=https://archive.org/details/classificationof0007louk |url-access=registration |publisher=UCLA Latin American Center |year=1968 |location=Los Angeles}}</ref> Glottolog, following Fabre (2005), treats Xukuru and Paratió as dialects.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Glottolog 5.1 - Xukurú |url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/xuku1239 |access-date=2025-04-10 |website=glottolog.org}}</ref>

==Distribution==
[[Geraldo Lapenda]] (1962) reported that the Xukuru people can be found primarily in the settlements of Canabrava and [[Brejinho]] in the ''aldeia'' of [[Cimbres]], [[Pesqueira, Pernambuco|Pesqueira]] municipality. They can also be found in the settlements of [[Cajueiro]], Ipanema Velho, Caldeirão, Jitó, Lagoa, Machado, Sitio do Meio, Riacho dos Afetos, Trincheiras, Bem-te-vi, Santana, and São José. Although the Xukuru traditionally occupied the [[Serra do Ororobá]], they could also be found in other municipalities of [[Pernambuco]], namely [[Caruaru]], [[Brejo da Madre de Deus]], [[Belo Jardim]], [[Sanharó]], [[Poção]], [[Pesqueira, Pernambuco|Pesqueira]], and [[Arcoverde]].<ref name="Lapenda-Xucuru"/>

==Other languages with this name==
	
''Xukuru-Kariri'' is a variety of [[Xokó language|Xokó]], which may be a [[Kariri languages|Kariri language]]. The name ''Kiriri'' is shared by [[Dzubukuá language|Dzubukuá]], another Kariri language, and by [[Katembri language|Katembri]]. The name ''Kiriri-Xoko'' is shared with yet another variety of Xokó.

Xukuru also has nasalized vowels. Lapenda (1962) transcribes nasalized vowels as ''Vn'' (orthographic vowel followed by ''n''). Descending diphthongs are attested, but only for oral vowels.<ref name="Lapenda-Xucuru" />

==Morphology==
Common suffixes in Xukuru include -'''''go''''', which forms verbs, adjectives, and nouns, and -'''''men''''', of uncertain meaning.<ref name="Lapenda-Xucuru"/>
